content.todaysFocus: Week 6 is the first sustainable inflection point: the crying curve is at or just past peak, and Avi is now smiling spontaneously at faces. Today's lever is a one-time setup task with a multi-year payoff: decide on a first instrument and start passive listening exposure.

actionItems.body: Decide on a first instrument with Noah and Anoushka today: violin (Suzuki's original), piano, or cello. The choice mostly sets which recordings you order; formal lessons are still about three years out, around age 3-4.
Order the Book 1 and Book 2 listening recordings for that instrument. Daily passive listening from this age carries no downside and is the single highest-leverage Suzuki prep step.
Schedule Avi's 2-month well visit if it is not yet booked; the window is day 56-70 and the rotavirus first dose must land by about day 104, so do not let it drift.

watchFors: [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds and wet sneezing are normal autonomic noise at this age and need no action.
[monitor] No social smile yet. About 80% of infants smile spontaneously by 8 weeks; if absent by then, flag it at the 2-month visit rather than now.
[monitor] Forceful arching or painful spit-up after feeds. Document frequency and discuss reflux or cow's-milk-protein intolerance at the next visit.
[call within 24h] A cluster of new symptoms together: poor feeding plus unusual lethargy plus decreased wet-diaper output.

[call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, a pause in breathing, blue color around the lips, or seizure-like activity: call the pediatrician same-day, and dial 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

enrichment.body: Play the new Suzuki recording softly during quiet play and feeds; aim to build toward roughly 30 minutes a day of background listening over the coming months. Live, participatory music matters more later, but early ear exposure is the Suzuki mother-tongue premise.
Build toward 30 minutes a day of tummy time across several short bouts as Avi now sustains 30-60 second head lifts. Distribute it after alert wake windows rather than after feeds.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

enrichment.body: Read aloud with intentional pauses: read a line, look at him, pause, then read the next line. The serve-and-return cadence is the active ingredient even before he can talk and predicts later expressive language.

content.todaysFocus: Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit is days away, and it is a high-value, easy-to-underprepare appointment. Today is about writing the question list so nothing gets skipped in a 20-minute slot.

actionItems.body: Draft Anoushka's written question list for the 6-week OB visit covering pelvic floor symptoms, mood and a repeat depression screen, return to exercise, and contraception. A written list is the difference between a thorough visit and a rushed one.
Add a contraception decision to the list. Progestin-only options (mini-pill, IUD, implant) are breastfeeding-compatible; combined estrogen products are usually deferred until weaning.
Note the return-to-work date and a daycare or nanny start date on the same list so the OB conversation and household logistics stay aligned; aim for a 1-2 week buffer between the two.

watchFors: [low concern] A quiet startle to loud sounds and a brief whole-body twitch as he drifts off are normal and need no action.
[monitor] For Anoushka: lochia alba persisting past 6 weeks, or red bleeding reappearing for a day or two. Note it for the OB visit.
[call within 24h] For Anoushka: incision redness or discharge, foul-smelling lochia, or one-sided calf pain. For Avi: a new murmur or blue color around the lips during feeds.
[call within 24h] Soaking more than one pad an hour for over two hours, which can signal delayed postpartum hemorrhage.

[call now] Avi with a rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, or seizure-like activity; or Anoushka with chest pain, shortness of breath, or thoughts of self-harm: get same-day help, and call 911 for breathing trouble!

enrichment.body: Refresh the high-contrast card set and hold each card 8-12 inches from his face; he now smiles spontaneously, especially at faces, so pair the cards with your own exaggerated expression.

Narrate ordinary tasks in parentese, the slow high-pitched register infants prefer: describe the diaper change, the dishwashing, the walk in full sentences. Rich responsive talk in infancy predicts later language outcomes.

Take a 20-30 minute stroller walk in daylight most days. It supports Anoushka's cardiovascular recovery and gives Avi varied sensory input, though it does not replace the 400 IU/day vitamin D supplement recommended for breastfed infants.

subject: Day 37: plan a Cal Academy outing

content.todaysFocus: With the crying peak easing, a short low-stimulation outing is now realistic and good for both parents and baby. Today is about planning one well-timed trip rather than improvising one on a crowded afternoon.

actionItems.body: Plan a low-stimulation weekday morning at the California Academy of Sciences; arrive at opening to avoid crowds and noise, and keep the loop short enough that you can leave before Avi tips into overstimulation.
Pack the outing bag the night before with a feed's worth of milk, a spare outfit, and the carrier, so a fussy morning does not cancel the plan.
Confirm the 2-month well visit is on the calendar for the day 56-70 window if you have not already booked it; the rotavirus first dose has a hard upper age limit around day 104.

watchFors: [low concern] Evening fussiness with no clear cause; the witching-hour pattern around 5-8pm is normal and tapering this week.
[monitor] Cradle cap (yellow scale on the scalp) or continuous tearing from one eye without redness (a blocked tear duct). Both are common and usually resolve without treatment.
[call within 24h] Persistent inability to console combined with arching during feeds, which can point to reflux or cow's-milk-protein intolerance.
[call within 24h] Forceful, projectile vomiting paired with poor weight gain.
[call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, blue lips, or inconsolable crying with a fever: call same-day, and dial 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

enrichment.body: Set a baby-safe mirror at Avi's eye level during tummy time; face-tracking is the strongest motivator for longer head lifts and helps build toward the 30 minutes-a-day target.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

enrichment.body: Play the Suzuki recording softly for 5-10 minutes during quiet play to keep the daily listening habit going without crowding out live singing.
Wear Avi in a carrier outside with his face visible and chin off his chest. Upright outdoor time gives him a changing field of light, sound, and motion that floor play cannot.

content.todaysFocus: Reading aloud is one of the highest-effect-size early-language interventions, and at this age repetition does the work. Today is about locking in a small fixed book set rather than chasing variety.

actionItems.body: Set a fixed rotation of three to five board books and read them daily; repetition, not novelty, is the vehicle for predictive language processing at this age. High-contrast and rhythmic-text titles work best now.
Order or borrow any missing staples for the rotation; a library card is free from birth and lets favorites repeat without buying every title.
Confirm Avi's 2-month well visit is booked in the day 56-70 window; the visit anchors the first vaccine round and should not slip past day 70.

watchFors: [low concern] Frequent hiccups after feeds and occasional wet sneezing; neither needs intervention.
[monitor] No social smile by 8 weeks. Most infants reach it earlier; if it is missing by then, raise it at the 2-month visit.
[monitor] A persistent head tilt to one side with limited rotation may be positional torticollis; mention it at the next visit for a possible PT referral.
[call within 24h] Poor feeding plus lethargy plus a clear drop in wet-diaper output as a cluster.
[call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, blue color around the lips, or seizure-like activity: call the pediatrician same-day, and call 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

enrichment.body: Keep the same three to five board books in daily rotation and re-read them often; predictable repetition is what drives early predictive language processing, so resist the urge to constantly swap titles.
Smile and make eye contact to get Avi's attention, then wait for him to smile back. The social smile is consolidating this week, and these face-to-face exchanges reinforce it.
Prop Avi on a rolled towel under his chest for tummy time so his arms clear the floor; the slight incline lowers the effort of each head lift and keeps prone minutes accruing toward 30 a day.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

content.todaysFocus: Tummy time is the prescribed counterweight to back-sleeping, but floor sessions often draw protest at 6-10 weeks. Today is a lower-effort variant that keeps prone time accruing when the floor is a fight.

actionItems.body: Drape Avi across your forearm in a football hold as a low-protest tummy-time substitute when floor time turns fussy; it still loads the neck and upper body and counts toward the daily total.
actionItems.sourceLabel: AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

actionItems.body: Keep limiting container time (bouncer, swing, car seat outside the car) to under two hours a day so floor and prone practice is not crowded out.
actionItems.sourceLabel: AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

actionItems.body: Confirm the 2-month well visit is on the calendar; with Anoushka's postpartum visit landing this week, lock both appointments in together while the schedule is open.

watchFors: [low concern] Hating floor tummy time at 6-10 weeks is normal; shorten the bouts and pair them with your face or a song rather than dropping the practice.
[monitor] A head tilt that responds to repositioning is low-grade, but a tilt that persists despite varying his held and sleep positions warrants a mention at the 2-month visit.
[monitor] Forceful arching or painful, frequent spit-up during feeds; track it and raise reflux or milk-protein intolerance at the next visit.
[call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24h or refusal of several feeds in a row.
[call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, blue lips, limpness, or asymmetric movement on one side: call same-day, and dial 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

enrichment.body: Use the forearm football hold and across-the-lap incline as gentler tummy-time variants; rotating positions keeps prone time accumulating toward 30 minutes a day even on protest-heavy days.
enrichment.sourceLabel: AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play

enrichment.body: Take coo turns: when Avi vocalizes, respond as if he spoke, pause, wait for his next sound, then respond again. These proto-conversations are the serve-and-return pattern linked to stronger later language.
Slowly track a high-contrast card across his full visual field, side to side; by now he can follow an object roughly 180 degrees, and this exercises smooth visual pursuit.
